items.q: What are Tina Huang's three Obsidian + AI levels?
items.a: **L1 AI second brain** — you write, AI retrieves and interprets. **L2 AI database** — agents write, you or another agent query. **L3 LLM wiki** — AI writes, maintains, and retrieves; you source and ask. Axis is **who writes vs who retrieves**, not vector/graph sophistication.

items.q: Which level should a non-note-taker start at?
items.a: **Level 2.** Tina is a self-rated **3/10** note-taker. Life Bot logs food photos, Taco Bot writes process docs, widgets dump pomodoros — then she asks how to sequence deep work from that pile.

items.q: What does Level 1 look like on her YouTube vault?
items.a: **Claude Cowork** reads the whole vault: she does not have a concept-generation problem; six filter criteria already live in the notes. **Codex** turns the same corpus into an "is this worth filming?" checklist. Private path: Hermes / DeepSeek harness / OpenCode.

items.q: What is the Level 2 write bus?
items.a: **Obsidian Sync** (E2E, one of the few paid features) so agents on a PC, Mac Studio, and VPS write the same vault. Writer models: Gemini Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, local **Qwen 3.6 36B**.

items.q: How does she stand up a Level 3 wiki in practice?
items.a: New Hermes profile + **LLM wiki skill** + Telegram as ingest port — she claims **under 5 minutes**. Same Karpathy pattern: raw / wiki / schema; ingest, query, lint; `index.md` + `log.md`. Claude Code has the most clone-ready repos; the gist is intentionally vague.

sections.title: Vs Nate and vs the quiz

items.q: How does this differ from Nate's five second-brain levels?
items.a: Nate's ladder is **retrieval sophistication** (router → wiki → vectors → graphs → always-on). Tina's is **authorship**. Her L3 is roughly Nate L2 plus always-on ingest/lint. Her L2 (agents logging into markdown) is a write-side pattern Nate does not name.

items.q: What three Obsidian features make it AI-friendly?
items.a: She quizzes and never answers. Implied from the demo: **local markdown** any model can open; **wikilinks/graph**; **folder + Sync/plugins** as a shared store. Vault = IDE, LLM = programmer, files = codebase.
